items.text: The home page is simpler, with a shorter form for starting a chat.
Chats started from the home page use end-to-end encryption and easy-to-share links by default. PIN protection is optional and uses six digits.
Groundwork for faster live updates, so new messages can show up in a fraction of a second. It is switched off for now while we test it.
The GIF picker on phones shows fewer, larger GIFs in two columns, so they are easy to see and tap.
Opening a chat no longer puts the cursor in the message box. Turn on Focus the message box in Settings if you want it.
Each chat installs as its own app, so you can install several chats on a computer without them opening in each other.
Adding an encrypted chat to your Home Screen now keeps the full link, so the icon opens the chat straight away.
The version number in the footer now opens these release notes.
Adding a chat to your phone's Home Screen now keeps the chat link and its name, so the icon opens that exact chat.
When you create an event chat you can set up a welcome screen right away: a banner image, a welcome text and suggested messages.
You can keep typing while the banner image is being read, and a failed part now tells you which one and why.
Quiet chats now use far fewer resources while you wait for new messages, which keeps busy events smooth.
Chats get a readable link by default, like weekend-plans plus a few characters, with a live preview while you create the chat.
Plain links keep working, and you can still turn the friendly link off when you create a chat.
The encryption explainer on the create form is now a small info icon with a popover, so the form stays short.
Chat admins can change the PIN in Settings. Everyone else enters the new PIN the next time they open the chat.
Admins can add a banner image and up to six suggested messages to the welcome card. Tapping a suggestion fills the composer without sending it.
Long welcome texts now scroll inside the card, so the prompts and the Got it button stay reachable.
Slow mode limits how often each person can post. Admins are exempt.
Admins can mute or remove a member from a message, lock the chat so only the admin posts, and end a live event right away.
Remove and change the PIN keeps a removed person out for good in PIN chats.
Long names now wrap inside the organizer buttons and errors show next to the controls.
The product name is now written HopIn.chat everywhere: the app, link previews, the poster and the legal pages.
New home page wordmark: HopIn with a small .chat tucked underneath.
A switch on the create form makes an end-to-end encrypted chat. The key lives only in the invite link, and the share dialog, QR code and poster include it.
A lock icon in the header shows the chat is encrypted, with a plain-language sheet explaining what is and is not protected.
A reminder to save your full link, plus a way to forget the key on a device.
Business name colours on the home page.
A small cookie notice that never blocks the page. HopIn.chat only uses essential cookies.
Export an encrypted chat to Markdown or JSON. It is decrypted in your browser.
AI recap in encrypted chats asks for your consent each time before anything leaves your browser.
Welcome messages work in encrypted chats, and link previews load only when you tap Load preview.
Security hardening.
Images, PDFs, documents, voice notes and GIFs are now encrypted in your browser before upload in encrypted chats.
Previews for encrypted files open straight from your device, and a failed download offers a Retry button.
Security hardening.
Security hardening of chat sign-in and PIN storage. Admins can sign everyone out of a chat.
Switching a chat between open and PIN now signs out the old members.
Print a QR poster or table tent from the Share dialog, or save it as an image, so people can scan to join.
In encrypted chats, messages, edits, replies, threads and polls are encrypted in your browser. Our server cannot read them.
A new Events page and an event preset when you create a chat.
Set a start and end time. Before the start and after the end only the admin can post, and old messages are cleared a day after the event.
Chats can have a friendly address based on their name. It is shown and shareable from the chat, and the original link keeps working.
First groundwork for end-to-end encryption.
A full design pass: consistent spacing, cards, inputs, buttons and sheets across the app.
Report a message to the chat admin, who can review and dismiss reports.
Block someone to hide their messages on your device.
Admins can pin a welcome message that new members see when they join.
Chats no longer need a PIN. Create an open chat that anyone with the link can join.
Each chat has an admin. Only the creator can delete the chat, and everyone can leave.
Security hardening for open chats.
More space between the PIN field and the Terms checkbox on the create card.
On phones: swipe a message to reply, and a touch-friendly action sheet for each message.
Dialogs on phones now open as bottom sheets.
The composer hides Markdown markers and shows only the styled text.
Better phone support: safe areas, keyboard handling and a one-row composer.
Private chat rooms with an optional PIN: one link, no accounts and no installs.
Voice messages, polls, threads, pinned messages, reactions and an emoji search with skin tones.
Image and document previews, link previews, and export to Markdown or JSON.
Read receipts and delivery ticks, a share dialog with QR code, and an installable app that works offline.
Terms and Privacy pages, a refreshed HopIn.chat logo and a compact phone header.
